newsitem.title: UK: INLA guerrillas' political arm rejects IRA truce.
newsitem.headline: INLA guerrillas' political arm rejects IRA truce.

text.p: The political wing of a small but deadly anti-British guerrilla group in Northern Ireland, the INLA, said on Monday that a truce called at the weekend by the IRA would not help end British "occupation" in the province.

The Irish Republican Socialist Party (IRSP) said in a statement that the truce, which will allow the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing to sit at peace talks sponsored by Britain and Ireland, would not help get the united Ireland both it and the IRA seek.
It was the first time the IRSP had commented on the Irish Republican Army's weekend statement calling a halt to its 28-year campaign of violence against British rule of Northern Ireland.
The IRSP is the political voice of the Irish National Liberation Army, which broke away from the IRA in the 1976 and is seen as an extreme Marxist group with small but fanatical support.

"It is our view that the so-called peace process is little more than a thinly veiled attempt at pacifying Nationalist demands while neutralising Republican resistance to the British occupation of Ireland," it said.
"This analysis is shared by a vast majority of grass-roots republican supporters and activists," the statement said.
The IRSP "recognises and applauds the tenacity and bravery of IRA volunteers over the years of repression and resistance", the statement said.

The INLA never declared a ceasefire in its war against Britain. It claimed responsibility for several shooting attacks on Northern Ireland security personnel during riots this month over annually held Protestant Orange Order parades.

It also claimed credit for a 1979 bombing at the car park of Britain's parliament which killed Conservative legislator Airey Neave, a confidant and aide of Margaret Thatcher before she became Britain's prime minister a few months later that year.
